ms.report:
A. Output: Social accounts for development updates — a Twitter/X account and a Discord server for the project (Epora).
Acceptance criteria: Twitter/X: basic account exists and is active. Discord: server with an open join option (permanent invite link, does not expire) and a general section where members can interact.
Evidence: Twitter/X: https://x.com/schaier_io
(changed due to weird x suspended account glitch, with a successful appeal that still shows as suspended)
Discord (permanent invite, lands in the general channel): https://discord.gg/2uh4BynQBW
Both are also linked from the project README: https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet

B. Output: Final whitepaper (v1.0), published as PDF with full LaTeX source in the public repository.
Acceptance criteria: Contains an Abstract (page 2) and an Introduction (Section 1). Explains the general functionality: Section 2 (EUTXO background) and Section 4 (System Architecture — features as configuration, state-thread token, two-validator handshake, datum-free receiving, stake-credential pinning). Explains how the permission system works and which permissions are possible: Section 5 (Permission and Recovery Model) with the full transition table (owners, weighted multi-signature, per-day spending allowances, proof-of-life dead-man-switch, weighted-share beneficiary recovery, streaming payments) and the State configuration fields in Section 4. Shows example use-cases: Section 9 (Illustrative Use Cases — inheritance/backup, inheritance with vesting, shared treasury with allowances, plus the threat scenarios each configuration contains).
Evidence: https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet/blob/main/whitepaper/whitepaper.pdf
(LaTeX source in the same folder: https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet/tree/main/whitepaper)

C. Output: Detailed development tasks in the project tracker — a general overview of the tasks needed to build the prototype, broken down per milestone.

・Smart contract 
・Based on whitepaper
・On-chain part only
・Extensive documentation
・Testing to ensure security of funds
ms.criteria:
The acceptance criteria will be based on the code submitted
・Smart contract includes the methods described in the whitepaper

ms.report:
A. Output: Smart contract

The complete smart-contract implementation has been delivered in Aiken. It includes the state-thread token, two-validator handshake, operator and multisignature actions, allowances, proof-of-life renewal, beneficiary recovery, streaming payments, consolidation, access removal, staking and governance actions.
Acceptance criteria: Smart contract includes the methods described in the whitepaper.
Evidence:
Smart-contract source on main:
https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet/tree/main/code/smart-contract
On-chain validators on main:
https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet/tree/main/code/smart-contract/validators
Completed Milestone 2 checklist:
https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet/blob/main/tasks/milestone-2-smart-contract.md
B. Output: Based on whitepaper

The contract architecture and supported transitions were implemented from the project whitepaper. The completed checklist maps the whitepaper architecture, permission model and transaction methods to their implementations and tests.
Acceptance criteria: Smart contract includes the methods described in the whitepaper.
Evidence:
Whitepaper on main:
https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet/blob/main/whitepaper/whitepaper.pdf
Whitepaper-to-implementation checklist:
https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet/blob/main/tasks/milestone-2-smart-contract.md
Contract interaction and transition map:
https://github.com/schaier-io/epora-wallet/blob/main/code/smart-contract/INTERACTIONS.md
C. Output: On-chain part only

The on-chain validator layer is complete. It contains the state-thread validator, wallet validator, reference-store validator, on-chain data types, transition rules and security guards. The compiled Plutus blueprint is published with the source code.
Acceptance criteria: Smart contract includes the methods described in the whitepaper.
